_meta.format: F2 structured-input interpretation cards with two fixed, labeled target-language options and concise English metalinguistic feedback
source_evidence: docs/GRAMMAR_STRATEGY.md §§3b and 4 (structured input; form is the only cue to meaning)
docs/research/error-profiles/fr.md §§2.10 and 6 (15 recorded passé composé/imparfait selection errors; keep the target small)
_meta.provenance: Fifty newly authored, bank-attested seed items in standard French; no learner sentences or personal data are reproduced.
_meta.language_policy: sentence, question, options, answer, and contrast_form are French; why is concise English metalinguistic feedback.
_meta.validation_notes: All 50 source frames are distinct; no contrast_form is repeated as another source sentence. Exactly 25 sources use imparfait and 25 use passé composé. Apart from grammatically required auxiliary, participle, agreement, and je/j’ elision, each contrast changes only target verbal morphology. No time adverb, duration phrase, habitual-frequency expression, completion predicate, or surrounding event independently supplies the aspect reading. Passé composé is described as bounded/perfective, not as proof that every real-world consequence is complete; imparfait is an internal/background view without an asserted endpoint. Content order and correct labels are stored in a frozen, deterministic constrained permutation; labels are cross-balanced by source tense, have no short repeated cycle, and never run more than three times consecutively.
_meta.ordering_policy: Frozen deterministic constraint-solved permutation v2 (seed 190); label and source-category streams reject runs longer than three, six-position period-2 windows, and nine-position period-3 windows in the full sequence and relevant routed subsequences.
